week.weeklyOverview: Toddlers meet everyday helpers—teachers, doctors, firefighters, mail carriers, and builders—through short imitation games, parallel dramatic play, and oversized props. Experiences stay brief and concrete: try on a hat, deliver one letter, gently check a teddy, then move on. Unlike preschool community units, this week emphasizes parallel play, simple thank-you language, and large materials rather than maps, interviews, or multi-step workshops.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Helper dress-up hats (firefighter, builder, doctor—toddler-sized)
Toy stethoscope and soft bandage rolls
Soft hose prop / short pool noodle section
Toy mailbags and large envelopes
Mailbox prop with wide slot
Friend photo cards for deliveries
Helper picture cards
Large soft blocks and toy trucks
Toy tools (chunky, no sharp edges)
Stuffed animals for rescue/clinic play
Washable paint, sponges, and large thank-you cardstock
Scarves for parade waves
Floor mats and clear parade path markers
week.teacherPreparation: Prep one tray at a time at toddler height. Keep Community Helpers materials chunky, washable, and mouthing-safe.
week.familyConnection: On walks or errands, point out one helper you see—“The mail carrier brings letters” or “The nurse helps people feel better.” At home, invite your toddler to pretend-check a stuffed animal or deliver a drawing to a family member. Practice saying thank you together for helpers who care for your family.
milestones: Language: Names or points to familiar helpers and uses help/thank-you words with support
SEL: Shows caring actions in pretend play (gentle checkup, soft rescue) and practices gratitude
Motor: Carries oversized props, posts large envelopes, marches in a short parade, and stacks large blocks
Cognition: Matches a helper tool to a helper role in simple one-step games

songs.title: Helpers Help Us Chant
songs.motions: Wave; tip an imaginary hat; show open caring hands; blow a thank-you kiss or wave at the end.
songs.teacherDirections: Hold one helper card per verse repetition. Keep to two minutes. Invite toddlers to choose a hat to hold while chanting—no need for full costumes.
songs.whenToUse: Opening circle and Thank You Helpers Parade Prep
songs.transitionPurpose: Introduce helper vocabulary and gratitude language
songs.lyrics:
Helpers help us every day,
Wave hello and on our way.
Hats and tools and caring hands,
Thank you, helpers, in our land.

songs.title: Stop and Go Helpers
songs.motions: March or slow scooter roll on green; freeze on red; hands on hips as proud helpers on safe.
songs.teacherDirections: Pair with Police Officer Stop and Go using large red/green signs. Keep speeds walking-slow. Celebrate freezes enthusiastically.
songs.whenToUse: Gross-motor helper games and outdoor transitions
songs.transitionPurpose: Practice body control with helper framing
songs.lyrics:
Green means go, we help and roll,
Red means stop—we self-control.
Helpers watch and keep us safe,
Stop and go at helper pace.

songs.title: Thank You March
songs.motions: March in place or along a short path; point to helper cards as named; big thank-you wave on the final line.
songs.teacherDirections: Use for Helper Hats Parade. Call only 2–3 helper names. End with bows—short and joyful.
songs.transitionPurpose: Celebrate helpers and close the week with gratitude
songs.lyrics:
March, march, thank you feet,
Smile at helpers down the street.
Doctor, teacher, firefighter too,
Thank you, thank you—we thank you!

teacherToolkit.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger toddlers explore with larger pieces; older peers get a second sorting rule or helper job.
teacherToolkit.extraSupportAdaptations: Sit beside, shorten the invitation, and offer hand-under-hand only when welcomed.
teacherToolkit.challengeExtensions: Invite children to invent a new Community Helpers rule, map, or story for peers.
teacherToolkit.safetyInclusionNotes: Use chunky, washable props without sharp tools or realistic scary emergency themes. Supervise dress-up to prevent trip hazards from oversized costumes—prefer hats over full suits. Ride-on stop-and-go stays slow with clear paths. Outdoor building uses soft/large blocks only. Paint activities need smocks and mouthing supervision. Keep play inclusive: helpers of many genders and roles are represented in photos and props.
teacherToolkit.endOfWeekReflection: Which Community Helpers words and strategies showed up most in play?
teacherToolkit.familyConnection: Share one Community Helpers word or song to try at home during ordinary routines.

legacySnapshot.weeklyOverview: Toddlers will learn about the people who help us every day in our homes, schools, and communities. Through dramatic play, books, songs, movement activities, and hands-on exploration, children will discover how helpers such as firefighters, doctors, teachers, farmers, mail carriers, and police officers make our communities safe and strong.
legacySnapshot.objectives:
- Identify community helpers and their roles
- Build vocabulary related to community jobs
- Encourage imaginative and dramatic play
- Strengthen communication skills
- Develop social awareness and appreciation for helpers
- Promote cooperation and problem-solving
